m1 - THE FIX IS VIABLE AND I HAVE SIZED IT. Scaling to ELIGIBLE weight rather than to all terms turns a 36% inflation into 4.7%, and makes your bit-identical law actually protect something.

MEASURED, default weights:

  SCALE OVER ALL TERMS (the ruling as written)
    5-term cell  1.3594     6-term cell  1.2985     <- nothing is ever bit-identical on WOG

  SCALE OVER ELIGIBLE TERMS (Chart and Structural ineligible: no charts exist in this corpus)
    eligible weight 3.35
    5-term cell  1.0469     6-term cell  1.0000     <- EXACTLY 1, bit-identical

So the eligible-aware version does what your first law promised. The fully-measured cells do not move at all, and the cells missing only Sensory inflate by 4.7% against the external floor rather than 36%. That is a plausible correction rather than a sign flip.

THE BLOCKER IS CONFIRMED AND IT IS NARROWER THAN I FEARED. Estimate has exactly two cases, Observed and Missing (features/estimate.scala:61-63). Undefined at :53 is a MissingReason, not a third arm. So the TYPE cannot say "this term was never eligible", which is precisely bd-01M16DBEH9PKER423BZ47ZKBMV.

BUT ELIGIBILITY IS DERIVABLE LOCALLY WITHOUT TOUCHING Estimate, and I think this is the way through:

  Structural is eligible iff the model has a provider - `structural` is a field of
  DefaultLocalCostModel (cost.scala:700) and defaults to StructuralDistance.missing. The cost model
  ALREADY KNOWS whether one was supplied.
  Chart is eligible iff the node carries evidence, which the view knows.

Neither needs a third Estimate arm. And the reason this is not the hidden convention I refused to build an hour ago is that THE ELIGIBLE SET GETS RECORDED IN CostBreakdown alongside the support weight - so it travels with the value, is inspectable, and can be refused. That is the ADR 0003 discipline rather than an exception to it. A convention becomes a contract the moment the artifact carries it.

SO THERE ARE TWO PATHS AND THEY ARE VERY DIFFERENT IN SIZE:
  (a) LOCAL: derive eligibility in the cost model from its own configuration, record it in
      CostBreakdown, scale to eligible weight. Contained to align. Does not touch the 31 Estimate
      sites. My recommendation.
  (b) PORTABLE: add Ineligible to Estimate first, then consume it here. Correct in the long run,
      and it is the P2 you deferred this morning as too wide.

(a) does not preclude (b) - if Estimate later grows the arm, the cost model swaps its local
derivation for the typed one and the recorded field stays the same shape.

I have NOT built either. I built the all-terms version, measured it, reverted it, then measured the
eligible variant arithmetically and stopped. Reservations still held; tell me (a), (b), or neither
and I will act or release.
